scope: Theorem 8.1 (Moment and half-plane consequences) of the manuscript “Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks” (preprints/Renewal-and-changes-of-law-for-critical-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d179fa55e4b82fed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 50. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the independent-irreducible infinite walk, and for uniform strict bridges at every sufficiently large even center length n, both endpoint distance and maximum radius have positive-moment powers 3p/4: for either variable Rn, ERp n = n3p/4+o(1) (p > 0 fixed). The same holds for the vertex-bridge conventions of Section 4. For endpoint-free uniform walks in the plane or half-plane, the probability of maximum radius exceeding n3/4+ϵ is smaller than every fixed inverse power of n, for each fixed ϵ > 0. In the half-plane there is one natural-density-one set of lengths along which endpoint distance and maximum radius have exponent 3/4 in probability and all the preceding positive-moment exponents. Under the half-plane law of free center length n ≥ 1 with weights ρne−tn, length is t−1+o(1) and endpoint distance and maximum radius are t−3/4+o(1) in probability as t ↓ 0; their positive moments have the corresponding powers. At fixed bridge height h, the critical bridge length is h4/3+o(1) both in probability and in first mean.
